architectural_shifts: From clustering/anchor-based item selection to latent-space D-optimal selection
From a single-model estimator to a stacked ensemble over source pseudo-target folds with incumbent fallback
From a linear/embedding latent model to a logistic latent-ability model with upper-tail Fisher designs
benchmarks: Open LLM Leaderboard v2 per-item results (IFEval, BBH, MATH Lvl 5, GPQA, MuSR, MMLU-Pro)
HELM per-item results (MMLU, GSM8K, MATH, LegalBench, MedQA, CommonsenseQA)
reference_query_plan.central_topic: Selecting a small subset of benchmark items using source models' per-item binary results and predicting a new LLM's full-benchmark score and ranking, via a latent-ability model with D-optimal item selection and a model-assisted difference estimator stacked over source pseudo-target folds.
comparators: Anchor points (clustering of model response vectors, weighted-average estimate)
Active evaluation acquisition (learned adaptive item selection)
Instance-level success prediction from few reference instances (assessor models)
Benchmark prediction from fewer data analysis (comparison of methods; failure on strong/extrapolated models)
core_methods: Model-assisted difference estimator (survey-sampling style) for full-benchmark mean from a subset
D-optimal / Fisher-information item selection in a latent ability space
Logistic (IRT-style) latent-ability model fit on source-model x item binary matrix
NNLS stacking of estimators over source pseudo-target folds with source-only validation and fallback blend
Bagged / Laplace posterior-mean ability estimation with tail (strong-model extrapolation) residual correction

queries.query: Anchor Points: Benchmarking Models with Much Fewer Examples
queries.rationale: Anchor-point clustering selection is a direct baseline (delta_mae_vs_anchor_points reported) and a starter reference.

queries.query: tinyBenchmarks: evaluating LLMs with fewer examples
queries.rationale: Anchors plus IRT estimator; the IRT-style baseline in the run (delta_mae_vs_irt_style) maps to this literature.

queries.query: metabench sparse benchmark reasoning knowledge LLMs item response theory
queries.rationale: IRT information-based item selection with a learned predictor; closest prior to Fisher-information item selection used here.

queries.query: Active Evaluation Acquisition for Efficient LLM Benchmarking
queries.rationale: Adaptive/learned item selection predicting remaining outcomes; contrasts with the static source-data-driven design here.

queries.query: How Benchmark Prediction from Fewer Data Misses the Mark
queries.rationale: Compares benchmark prediction methods on the same Open LLM Leaderboard/HELM data and discusses failure for extrapolation; matches the strong-target degradation seen in the run.

queries.query: predicting success of new LLM on unseen instances from few reference instances assessor
queries.rationale: Instance-level predictor trained from reference-instance outcomes on HELM-Lite; related prediction-from-subset formulation.

queries.query: model-assisted survey estimation difference estimator generalized regression estimator
queries.rationale: The core estimator is a model-assisted difference estimator (model prediction plus subset residual correction); needs survey-sampling grounding.

queries.query: D-optimal experimental design Fisher information logistic regression optimal item selection
queries.rationale: Item selection is D-optimal on latent features using logistic Fisher information; needs optimal-design and IRT test-design grounding.

queries.query: stacked generalization non-negative least squares combining predictors
queries.rationale: Final estimator stacks candidate estimators with NNLS weights over source pseudo-target folds.

queries.query: Open LLM Leaderboard v2 IFEval BBH MMLU-Pro GPQA MuSR benchmarks
queries.rationale: Data come from per-item Open LLM Leaderboard v2 results and HELM; benchmark citations needed for dataset description.

result_driven_themes: Estimation error and rank correlation degrade much more for strong (out-of-range) target models than for randomly held-out targets (strong_targets MAE roughly 2x random_targets; Spearman ~0.77-0.82 vs ~0.96)
Gains over random-subset and anchor-point baselines are small in absolute MAE terms (about 0.007-0.011) but consistent across the three variants
Source-only validation / stacking for extrapolation to targets above the source ability range
Posterior-mean and tail-calibration did not improve over plain logistic Fisher D-opt stacking (0.9445 vs 0.9452 combined score)
